pages.title: About Kogu Hardware
pages.content:
Since 1987

About Kogu Hardware

Kogu Hardware has served the Wrenfield community from 14 Alder Row since Mart Kogu first opened the doors in 1987. Today his daughter Liis Kogu runs the shop, preserving the single wooden counter and its wall of numbered drawers.

Opening on Alder Row in 1987

Mart Kogu founded Kogu Hardware in 1987 on 14 Alder Row in Wrenfield. He built the counter by hand, believing that a hardware shop should be organized around direct advice rather than long aisles of blister packs. From the start, the counter served as a practical meeting place for neighbours needing a single bolt, a replacement sash cord, or a key cut cleanly on the manual bench. Mart stood behind the timber counter six days a week, helping local residents diagnose household maintenance problems and showing them how to fix things themselves with reliable tools and proper fittings.

Visit the counter

One Counter and 1,248 Drawers

Behind our single timber counter sits a continuous wall containing 1,248 numbered drawers. Instead of forcing customers to wander through crowded aisles searching for fasteners, we keep every hinge, screw, washer, and fitting catalogued behind the desk. When you tell us what you are working on, we pull the specific drawer, lay the pieces on the timber surface, and explain how the hardware functions. This system ensures you buy the exact number of pieces required for your job rather than a plastic box of spares you will never need again.

Generations of Care and Repair Visits

In 2014, Liis Kogu took over the management of the shop from her father Mart. While preserving the core traditions and the 1,248 drawers, Liis expanded our direct assistance to include scheduled home repair visits within 3 km of 14 Alder Row. If a task requires hands-on help that cannot be brought to the counter, our team visits local homes to fix sticking doors, replace tap washers, or secure loose hardware. Mart remains an active presence in the business, frequently working Saturdays at the key bench.

Seven people. One counter.

Every one of them can walk to the right drawer.

Our shop is staffed by seven knowledgeable people dedicated to practical maintenance. Mart Kogu, who founded the shop in 1987, is at the key bench on Saturdays to duplicate keys and discuss older hardware. Liis Kogu manages counter service and purchasing. Yusuf Demir handles keys and lock cylinders. Tomás Reyes conducts our home repair visits within 3 km. Priya Nair oversees wood finishes and paints. Samuel Okoro manages the trade counter and commercial accounts. Hanna Berg runs our cutting room and teaches the Saturday fixing class.

pages.title: Home Fixers
pages.content:
Who comes in

Home Fixers

We help homeowners and renters solve common household maintenance problems with straightforward advice and exact parts. Bring your worn or broken item to our counter at 14 Alder Row, and we will find the match.

Bring the Broken Part to the Counter

The easiest way to resolve a household repair is to remove the old component and bring it directly to our shop. Whether you are dealing with a stripped screw, an unfamiliar latch, or a split rubber washer, seeing the physical part allows us to check the thread pitch, diameter, and clearance instantly. If the item cannot be removed safely, take a clear photograph with a coin placed beside it for scale. We will inspect the wear and locate the correct replacement from our drawers.

Drawers Home Fixers Open Most

drawers home fixers open most

Several of our 1,248 drawers are opened multiple times every day by local residents. Drawer 214 holds solid brass butt hinges in pairs for $12, perfect for rehanging cabinet doors or internal passage doors. Drawer 088 contains our traditional brass cabinet latch with keeper for $18, widely used on timber cupboards and older sash windows. Drawer 301 provides a tin of 220 stainless wood screws for $14, giving you a dependable selection of rust-resistant fasteners for timber frames and shelving repairs.

pages.title: Makers & Schools
pages.content:
Who comes in

Makers & Schools

We provide timber preparation, daily tool hire, and practical workshop space for independent makers, craftspeople, and educational institutions in Wrenfield. Our cutting room and hardware drawers supply the raw materials and advice you need to build.

Cut to Size and Timber Preparation

Our rear workshop features a precision panel saw and cutting table operated by Hanna Berg. We cut plywood, timber boards, and sheet materials down to your specified dimensions for $1.50 per cut. Rather than struggling with full sheets in a small studio, you can have your panels squared and trimmed accurately to size. We also supply reliable layout tools, including our classic two-metre beech folding rule from Drawer 640 for $16, helping you mark out joinery with confidence.

Cut, hire, learn

three ways to build

Tool Hire for Projects and Experiments

You do not need to purchase expensive machinery for temporary or specialized construction jobs. We maintain a fleet of dependable tools available for hire at a flat rate of $16 per day, including heavy-duty drills, electric sanders, and precision tile cutters. Each tool is inspected and tested between hires to ensure safe operation. Hanna Berg can demonstrate proper handling and setup at the counter, ensuring you have the right accessories and safety gear before starting your work.

The Saturday Fixing Workshop

Every Saturday morning from 10:00 to 12:00, Hanna Berg leads our community fixing class in the shop workshop. The workshop costs $20 per participant and is limited strictly to eight places to ensure personal attention and adequate workbench space. Participants learn how to handle hand tools, sharpen chisels, strip and replace tap washers, repair hinges, and complete basic timber joinery. All necessary materials, hand tools, and protective equipment are provided during the two-hour practical session.

We pre-cut timber components, pack fasteners into labeled batches, and coordinate collection or delivery within 3 km. By preparing sheet materials accurately and packaging the right brass latches and screws, we help educators spend their class time teaching hands-on skills rather than preparing rough timber.

pages.title: Solid Brass Butt Hinges, 75 mm, Pair
pages.content:
Drawer 214

Solid Brass Butt Hinges, 75 mm, Pair

Drawer 214

$12

Pulled from Drawer 214 behind our counter, these 75 mm solid brass butt hinges provide lasting strength for internal timber doors and joinery. Each pair is priced at $12 and is supplied with matching countersunk brass screws.

Click & collect free · Local delivery within 3 km $6 (free over $60) · Returns within 30 days

Reserve by phone: (555) 014-1987

Product Description and Materials

These solid brass butt hinges from Drawer 214 are machined from extruded brass for superior durability and corrosion resistance. Measuring 75 mm in height, they are designed for internal residential doors, cupboard frames, and substantial cabinet work. Unlike steel-plated alternatives that rust or bind over time, solid brass wears evenly and develops a quiet, natural patina. Each pair includes matching solid brass slotted wood screws to ensure a neat, flush finish that sits perfectly flush in hardwood or softwood joinery.

How to Fit and Install at Home

Fitting these hinges requires careful morticing into the door edge and timber frame. Mark the hinge leaf outline with a sharp marking knife, then chisel out the timber recess to match the exact thickness of the brass leaf. Drill pilot holes for the brass screws using a suitable timber drill bit to prevent shearing the softer metal. If you need guidance on setting door clearances, our counter team can demonstrate the proper morticing technique on our sample timber block at 14 Alder Row.

Collection, Delivery, and Returns

You can pick up these hinges at our shop counter with our free click and collect service, available Monday through Saturday. If you prefer delivery to your home or worksite, we deliver within 3 km for $6, or free of charge when your order exceeds $60. If you discover you need a different hinge length or throw, return the hinges unused in their original condition with your purchase receipt within 30 days for an exchange or a complete refund.

pages.title: Stories from the Counter
pages.content:
From the shop

Stories from the Counter

A hardware shop collects practical stories of old fixtures, school projects, and early morning trade runs. Here are four genuine accounts from the counter at 14 Alder Row in Wrenfield.

Home fixers

A Latch from 1962

A renter living on Birch Street came to the counter holding an old, broken window latch from a 1962 casement frame.

Makers & schools

Forty Pieces for a School Stage

When Wrenfield Primary began building their annual school play set, their drama department needed forty bespoke plywood panels cut accurately on a tight deadline.

Home fixers

The Tap That Dripped for a Year

A local homeowner visited the shop frustrated by a bathroom basin tap that had dripped continuously for twelve months.

A Latch from 1962

A renter living on Birch Street came to the counter holding an old, broken window latch from a 1962 casement frame. The landlord could not locate a matching piece, and standard hardware stores had suggested replacing the entire timber frame. Liis Kogu walked over to the drawer wall, opened Drawer 088, and produced our traditional brass cabinet latch with keeper for $18. The screw hole centers matched within half a millimeter, allowing the window to latch securely without altering the original woodwork.

Forty Pieces for a School Stage

When Wrenfield Primary began building their annual school play set, their drama department needed forty bespoke plywood panels cut accurately on a tight deadline. Hanna Berg took the cutting list into our rear cutting room and sized each panel cleanly on our panel saw at $1.50 per cut. The teacher and two student volunteers stacked the forty panels by the cutting room door and loaded them into a van, ready for assembly the next morning without sanding or trimming.

The Tap That Dripped for a Year

A local homeowner visited the shop frustrated by a bathroom basin tap that had dripped continuously for twelve months. Rather than recommending a costly replacement tap set, Liis Kogu placed a brass tap body on the counter and demonstrated how to isolate the water, unscrew the headgear, and swap the worn washer. The customer purchased our 40-piece tap washer kit from Drawer 512 for $9, returned home, and stopped the drip completely in less than ten minutes.

Read the full article

Saturday, 7:30

At 7:30 on a cold Saturday morning, a local plumbing contractor arrived at our trade entrance facing an emergency repair on a residential heating system. Samuel Okoro had arrived early to organize invoices and pre-pack commercial orders. Within five minutes, Samuel pulled the required fittings, brass padlocks, and stainless wood screws from Drawer 301, applied the contractor's ten percent trade discount, and sent the plumber on his way to site before the shop's public opening.

pages.title: How to Ask
pages.content:
At the counter

How to Ask

You never need to know the official technical name of a part when you visit our counter. Follow our four simple steps, or check our answers to common questions below.

Four steps at the counter

01

Bring the old part, or a photo with a coin beside it for scale.

02

Tell us what it does and where it lives.

03

We match it from the drawers and show you how to fit it at the counter.

04

If it doesn't fit, bring it back within 30 days.

Open Monday to Friday 7:30 to 18:30, Saturday 8:00 to 17:00, closed Sunday.

Questions at the counter

six answers

Do you cut car keys?

No, we do not cut electronic, transponder, or chipped automotive keys at our counter. We specialize exclusively in duplicating house keys, cylinder keys, mortice keys, and padlock keys. Standard keys are cut on our manual bench for $4.50 per key while you wait, and high-security or dimple keys are cut for $14 each upon presentation of the registered security card. For electronic vehicle keys, you will need to consult an automotive locksmith.

Can I bring a photo instead of the old part?

Yes, you can bring a photograph if the broken component cannot be removed safely from your wall or door. When taking the picture, place a common coin directly beside the hardware to provide an accurate scale reference, and take one shot from the front and one from the side. While holding the original physical part is always preferable for checking thread pitch and diameter, a clear scale photograph usually allows us to identify the correct replacement.

Do you deliver to my home or site?

Yes, we offer local delivery for all items in our 1,248 drawers, as well as cut timber and hired tools. We deliver to any address located within 3 km of our shop at 14 Alder Row in Wrenfield. Local delivery costs a flat fee of $6 per trip, and is provided completely free of charge for orders of $60 or more. Deliveries are typically scheduled on weekday afternoons or during early morning trade hours.

What is your returns policy?

We want you to feel confident that any part you purchase from our counter will solve your repair problem. If a hinge, latch, fastener, or plumbing seal does not fit your fixture, you may return it to our shop at 14 Alder Row within 30 days of purchase. Items must be unused, in their original condition, and accompanied by your sales receipt for a complete exchange or full refund to your original payment method.

How do I open a trade account?

Opening a trade account is quick and can be arranged directly at our trade desk with Samuel Okoro. Registered tradespeople and local businesses receive a ten percent discount off shelf prices across our entire inventory, along with thirty-day payment terms on monthly invoices. You can apply at the counter from 7:30 on weekday mornings by providing standard commercial identification and trade references, or review our trade terms on our Trade page.

Do you hire out tools?

Yes, we hire out reliable power tools and equipment for $16 per day to help you tackle demanding home and workshop tasks without buying machinery. Our hire fleet includes heavy-duty drills, electric sanders, and tile cutters. Every hired tool is cleaned, tested, and inspected between hires. You can reserve equipment at the counter or by phone at (555) 014-1987, and our staff will explain safe operating procedures before you leave.

posts.title: The Tap That Dripped for a Year
posts.excerpt: A Wrenfield homeowner stopped a year-long bathroom leak in ten minutes after learning how to replace a worn washer at our counter.
posts.content:
Drawer 512, $9, ten minutes.

Every neighbourhood hardware shop has a collection of quiet, persistent domestic grievances that customers carry to the counter. On a quiet Tuesday morning in Wrenfield, a resident walked through the door of 14 Alder Row with an expression of weary resignation. For twelve months, a basin tap in their upstairs bathroom had dripped continuously into the porcelain bowl. What had started as an occasional nocturnal click had settled into a steady, rhythmic cadence that wore away sleep and wasted litres of clean water. The homeowner had tried tightening the tap handle with increasing force, but the drip persisted, growing stubborn and indifferent to brute strength.

Like many renters and homeowners, the customer assumed the only permanent remedy was a full replacement of the plumbing fixtures. They had visited a regional home center where a salesperson suggested purchasing an entirely new brass mixer set, complete with braided hoses and a modern ceramic cartridge, costing well over a hundred dollars. Uncertain about cutting into supply pipes and reluctant to pay for unnecessary plumbing work, they decided to stop by Kogu Hardware to ask whether there was any simpler alternative.

Liis Kogu listened carefully to the description of the faucet, asking whether the drip flowed from the spout or leaked around the spindle collar. When the customer confirmed the water steadily escaped from the nozzle, Liis reached beneath the timber counter and produced a cutaway brass tap body used for customer demonstrations. In a hardware store with 1,248 drawers, the solution to a leaking tap is rarely a brand-new fixture; it is almost always a small disc of vulcanized rubber that costs less than a morning newspaper.

Standing at the wooden counter, Liis showed the customer how a traditional compression tap works. When you turn the handle, a threaded brass spindle drives a jumper valve down against a circular brass seat inside the tap body. Over time, friction, water pressure, and mineral deposits compress and groove the rubber washer, preventing it from forming a watertight seal. Cranking down harder on the handle does not stop the leak; it merely tears the tired rubber and risks scoring the brass seat underneath.

Liis pulled Drawer 512, which holds our 40-piece tap washer and O-ring kit, priced at $9. She laid out the replacement parts on the counter and walked the customer through the repair step by step. First, isolate the mains water supply or shut off the local isolation valve beneath the basin. Second, pop off the tap index cap and undo the retaining screw to lift off the handle. Third, use an adjustable wrench to unscrew the brass headgear nut. Finally, slide out the jumper valve, pop off the split washer, push on the fresh rubber disc, and reassemble.

The customer left 14 Alder Row with the $9 kit from Drawer 512 and our standard advice: if any part did not fit, bring it back within 30 days. Two hours later, they phoned the shop to report that the entire job had taken under ten minutes using an ordinary wrench, and the tap was now completely silent. That ten-minute repair is why Kogu Hardware has stood on Alder Row since Mart Kogu first opened the counter in 1987. We believe in keeping good things working, teaching people practical skills, and proving that the right part and patient advice will always outlast throwaway convenience.
